grok-4.5.o3-mini: Severely compresses and rearranges source events while inventing timing for the Real declaration; visuals are thin and scenes often cram multiple actions or rely on unfilmable memory floods, yielding weak short-clip pacing and only middling dialogue lift from the book.
grok-4.5.gpt-4o-mini: Reads as illustrated synopsis rather than screenplay; constant NARRATOR undercuts show-don't-tell, character looks are barely sketched, and pacing collapses into summary fragments unusable for 5-10s AI clips.
grok-4.5.grok-4: Faithful beat-for-beat coverage with near-verbatim Skin Horse and Fairy dialogue, clear recurring visual tags (pink sateen, bald patches, pearl dew-drops), and mostly single-action scenes that cut cleanly into short clips; minor density in a few transitions keeps it from perfection.
grok-4.5.claude-sonnet-5: Otherwise lush and nearly complete adaptation with excellent painterly casting locks and emotional arc, but the explicit naming of a wild rabbit as Bramble is an invented named character that disqualifies on the fidelity dimension regardless of other strengths.
grok-4.5.gemini-3.6-flash: Strong visual introductions and some filmable action, yet invented naming plus fabricated toy dialogue and minor event tweaks (butterfly chase, etc.) constitute clear fidelity violations that also dilute dialogue authenticity.
grok-4.5.grok-4.5: Near-perfect source coverage with every major beat and almost all original dialogue intact; every character carries locked, repeated visual descriptors usable for reference images; action lines are granular, single-clip observables with clean emotional escalation ideal for AI short-form video.
grok-4.5.gpt-4o: Functions as a high-level outline rather than a screenplay; dialogue is paraphrased into fragments, characters lack any casting-stable description, and there is no rhythm or observable action dense enough for short AI clips.
grok-4.5.gemini-2.5-flash: Highly faithful rendering of all key sequences and dialogue with solid recurring visual tags and well-paced escalation; slightly less granular clip-ready action lines and thinner sound-atmosphere cues than the top candidate keep it just below exceptional.

grok-4.gpt-4o: Heavy narrator reliance and some compressed beats reduce fidelity and directibility for short clips.
grok-4.o3-mini: Strong visual action lines and emotional beats, minor gaps in character consistency across time.
grok-4.grok-4.5: Exceptional fidelity and filmable beats with consistent descriptions; ideal for clip format.
grok-4.gemini-3.6-flash: Very faithful with clear visuals, slightly less nuanced pacing than C.
grok-4.claude-sonnet-5: Excellent directibility and source accuracy with strong subtext in short lines.
grok-4.gemini-2.5-flash: Solid coverage but some scenes cram actions and weaker character visual consistency.
grok-4.grok-4: Condensed structure loses some beats and directibility for clip-by-clip execution.
grok-4.gpt-4o-mini: Too summarized with heavy narration and insufficient visual action lines.

JudgeSummaries.grok-4.5: Strongest: Screenplay F because it delivers near-verbatim source fidelity, locked consistent character visuals, and the cleanest single-action beats optimized for 5-10s AI clips. Weakest: Screenplay G because it collapses the entire story into an undramatized synopsis lacking visuals, dialogue texture, and any usable clip structure.
JudgeSummaries.grok-4: Strongest: Screenplay C because it achieves near-perfect fidelity with highly filmable, single-action beats and consistent character visuals. Weakest: Screenplay H because heavy narration and vague descriptions make it unusable for short-clip AI video production.
